findings.claim: The compatibility guard suppresses ExcludeFromCodeCoverage on netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework even though ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute is available on those targets (including .NET Framework 4.0 and later). Consequently, generated code on supported targets compiled with NETSTANDARD2_0 or NETFRAMEWORK is not decorated, contrary to the requirement that all generated code be excluded except where the attribute must be conditionally omitted because it does not exist.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageTargetFrameworkTests.GeneratedTypes_RemainExcludedWhenTargetFrameworkSymbolsAreDefined. The test independently verifies that the attribute compiles against netstandard2.0, then inspects active generated declarations with NETSTANDARD2_0 and NETFRAMEWORK defined; it fails on head because the directives remove the attribute.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Decoration is unconditional and applies to every emitted formatter, resolver, and nested helper type whenever the attribute exists. Consumers need no setting, and no opt-out is introduced; this is the design implemented by the change apart from its target-framework exclusions.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Decoration is enabled by default but can be disabled through a new opt-out generator/MSBuild setting. The same generated types are decorated initially, while consumers who want generated code included in coverage can set the option to suppress emission of the attribute.
